commit.message: Add a PowerShell installer, because curl | bash is a Unix idiom

findings.title: Doctor searches only ~/.vscode/extensions while the extension searches five roots
findings.description: The header promises it "checks every precondition the extension checks, in the same order", but `engine/src/claude-cli.ts` scans .vscode, .vscode-insiders/.vscode-oss, .cursor, .cursor-server and .windsurf, and also probes `resources/claude.exe` and `bin/claude.exe` layouts. A Cursor or Windsurf user with a bundled Claude gets "no claude binary found anywhere this script looked" from the doctor while the extension finds it — the doctor then sends them off installing something they already have.
findings.suggestion: Mirroring the root list and the two fallback layouts from claude-cli.ts would keep the doctor's verdict aligned with what the extension actually does.

findings.title: Zip-header check throws instead of reporting on a short or empty download
findings.description: `[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($vsix)[0..1]` on a zero-byte file yields $null, and `$head[0]` then raises "Cannot index into a null array" under $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' — the user gets a red PowerShell exception rather than the friendly message this block exists to print. It also loads the whole multi-megabyte file to inspect two bytes.
findings.suggestion: Reading just the first two bytes off a stream and treating a short read as a failed download would keep the intended message on every path.

findings.title: "Try manually" points at a .vsix the finally block has already deleted
findings.description: When the post-install version check fails, the script prints a manual command referencing $vsix, then returns — and the enclosing `finally` immediately removes $tmp recursively, so the file is gone before the user can copy the command. The bash installer avoids this by never cleaning up its mktemp dir, which is why the same message works there.
findings.suggestion: Consider copying the .vsix somewhere durable (or skipping the cleanup) on this failure path before printing the command, so the suggested recovery step is actually runnable.

findings.title: Bundled-Claude lookup sorts extension folders lexically, not by version
findings.description: `Sort-Object Name -Descending` orders `anthropic.claude-code-1.9.0` above `anthropic.claude-code-1.10.0`, so on a machine with several versions left behind the stale one is picked. This is the same defect already recorded against `engine/src/claude-cli.ts:103-106`, now duplicated in both .ps1 scripts (`doctor.ps1:92-96` too).
findings.suggestion: Consider parsing the trailing version out of the folder name and sorting on it (falling back to a low version when it doesn't parse), so the newest bundled binary wins here and in doctor.ps1.

findings.title: publish-r2.js never uploads the .ps1 scripts, so the R2 copies are unreachable
findings.description: `dist-r2/publish-r2.js` uploads install.sh, doctor.sh, version.txt and the .vsix only. The two new .ps1 files sit in dist-r2 but are never published, so `irm <r2-host>/install.ps1 | iex` 404s; only the Vercel-served `dashboard/public` copies work. The header comment advertising the one-liner is accurate for Vercel but not for the R2 channel these files live in.
findings.suggestion: Either add install.ps1/doctor.ps1 to the upload list in publish-r2.js (alongside doctor.sh), or drop the dist-r2 copies so there is one obvious source of truth for the Windows path.

findings.title: Placeholder guard can never fire and doesn't match the sh placeholder
findings.description: $base defaults to a real host and nothing rewrites this file at publish time, so the branch is unreachable today. If it were later wired into publish-r2.js it still wouldn't fire: install.sh uses `REPLACE_WITH_R2_HOST`, which does not contain the substring `REPLACE_WITH_HOST` this test looks for.
findings.suggestion: Either align the token with install.sh's `REPLACE_WITH_R2_HOST` and default $base to the placeholder, or drop the branch as dead code.

findings.title: Installer's Claude probe list omits a path doctor.ps1 checks
findings.description: doctor.ps1 also probes `$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\local\claude.exe`; the installer's list stops one entry short. A user with that layout gets the "Claude CLI was not found" warning from the installer and an "ok" from the doctor moments later, which reads as one of the two being broken.
findings.suggestion: Keeping the two lists identical would avoid the contradictory advice.
